title: stop two tests asserting a contract the product never promised, and canonicalize the herding resolver
action: Two test-side corrections. Validation removed the product-mutation half of this cell's earlier draft — read why before you start. SITE 1 — packages/bee/tests/test_cli_cells.mjs:879 asserts `changedFiles[0] === path.join('.bee','backlog.jsonl')` against `git show --name-only` output. git always prints forward slashes on every platform; path.join yields backslashes on win32, so the assertion cannot pass there. The product is correct: its pathspec is only ever fed INTO git add, which accepts either separator. Fix the test — compare against the forward-slash form git actually emits, or normalize the observed value before comparing — and say in the trace which you chose and why. SITE 2 — packages/bee/tests/test_herding_cli.mjs compares BOTH `out.marker === markerFile(root)` (:70) and `out.main_root === root` (:71) with === against fs.realpathSync of a temp dir, while the resolvers return path.dirname of git's stdout with no normalization. Fix BOTH assertions, not just :71 — path.join normalizes separators but not short-name aliasing, so :70 fails for the same underlying reason. DO NOT CANONICALIZE THE RETURNED VALUE, which the earlier draft told you to do and validation refuted: skills/bee-herding/SKILL.md:142 and :303 derive the worktree grant key by string surgery on main_root's basename, and that key is what the merge command expects as its --id — changing the returned spelling changes the key. The safe shape is canonicalize FOR COMPARISON, never mutate what is returned. If you conclude a product change is warranted anyway, that is a finding to report, not a change to make here. DO NOT SHARE A HELPER INTO THE INTERLOCK: packages/bee/lib/herding.mjs:26-41 records that .claude/skills/bee-herding/scripts/dispatch-interlock.mjs is a standalone zero-bee-dependency script whose entire purpose is byte-for-byte agreement with its twin, and that calling into it from bee automation is forbidden in either direction. The earlier draft told you to reuse wpi-1's helper there — do not. EDIT THE SOURCE, NOT THE MIRROR: .claude/skills/... is an onboard-managed install target that this cell's own regen chain rewrites from skills/...; an edit to the mirror is silently reverted while release_manifest --check stays green, because that mirror is not among the hashed roots. If any change to the interlock is warranted, it lands in skills/bee-herding/scripts/dispatch-interlock.mjs and its twin must stay byte-identical. VERIFY MUST DISCRIMINATE: both legs of the earlier draft were green on the unmodified tree — measured. Make your corrected assertions genuinely exercise the mismatch (drive the comparison through a spelling the platform would report differently, using wpi-1's injection seam), and record a red-first proof for each site.

truths: the cells queue-submit assertion passes against the forward-slash form git actually emits on every platform, with the choice and its reason recorded
BOTH herding assertions (:70 marker and :71 main_root) compare canonically, using wpi-1's comparison rather than a second implementation

no product value changes: main_root's returned spelling is untouched, and the report states what the sweep found about consumers — including the SKILL.md grant-key derivation that depends on its basename
the interlock script and its twin remain byte-identical and dependency-free; any change to them lands in skills/, never in the .claude mirror
red-first evidence per site: the corrected assertion fails against a spelling the old form accepted, and passes after
the release-manifest regen chain ran inside this cell and release_manifest.mjs --check is green

Never import a shared helper into the interlock script, and never edit the .claude mirror

Never write a second path-comparison implementation

checks.evidence: The commit touches exactly four paths: the cell record, the release manifest, and the two test suites. Filtering that list for the herding resolver, the interlock or the .claude mirror returns nothing, and the last commits touching those files predate this cell. main_root's returned value is untouched.
No .claude path appears in the commit. The two interlock twins hash identically and diff clean, and the interlock's imports remain node builtins only — no bee helper was shared in.

Falsification at commit state in scratch: baseline 7 passed / 0 failed; with ALL THREE corrected assertions reverted to their pre-fix === form, also 7 passed / 0 failed — the red-first guard row PASSED with the old assertions restored. The guard constructs its own strings and never routes through the resolver output the fixed assertions compare, so it cannot detect the assertion regressing. Site 1 is the same shape: path.join and the forward-slash literal are already equal on this platform, so the reverted expectation still passes, and the added sanity assert compares a win32-joined constant against git's always-forward-slash stdout, which cannot fail on any platform or product state — a demonstration, not a proof. Additional defect: the guard's GREEN leg pins canonicalPathsEqual's unconditional POSIX backslash fold, which this cell's own report flags as a wpi-1 defect.

Both original assertions were replaced with canonical comparisons, plus a third site covering the interlock's marker. All three consume wpi-1's helper by import — no second comparison implementation was written.

The cells assertion compares with strict equality against the literal forward-slash form git emits, keeps the length pinned at one, and does not loosen to a substring or a normalize-both-sides comparison. A wrong file, an extra file, or a backslash form still fails.

The claim holds and was verified independently: the grant key in the skill doc is derived from the main_root returned by the worktree list command, which resolves through a different function than the herding resolver this cell was told not to touch; the herding resolver's only consumers are herding enable, disable and status. IMPLICATION FOR THE RECORD: the plan's correction justified 'never canonicalize main_root's returned value' by that grant key, and that reason points at the wrong resolver. The prohibition still stands for an independent reason that should replace it — a test asserts the bee resolver and the standalone interlock agree byte-for-byte on the marker, and sharing a helper into the interlock is forbidden, so canonicalizing only bee's side would break that agreement.

Scope is clean and the manifest regen genuinely ran — both test files' hashes match the stored manifest. But the judge's own runs are not green: the herding suite fails on the guard's GREEN row, the path-identity suite fails on its separator-fold row, and the manifest check reports one changed file. All three reds trace to wpi-1's uncommitted rework in the working tree, which now gates backslash folding on the platform separator — the replay at commit state was 7/7 green. That is precisely the coupling this cell introduced: its guard asserts the POSIX backslash fold as a contract, so wpi-1's correction turns wpi-2's own verify red.
